blocks.title: What Can You Do About a Two Year Old Child?

blocks.text: Parents of two year-old-children constantly struggle, searching for ways to survive that turbulent period known as the «terrible-two’s».

When your own two-year-old misbehaves, it’s usually because of his natural curiosity. It isn’t cruelty that causes him to thrust a pencil deep into the dog’s nostril, but a genuine desire to find out how you’ll react.
As a guide to parents we recommend the following graded threat sequence:

items: You’re going to get hurt or hurt somebody else.
You’re going to make me very angry.
You’re going straight to your room.
I’m going to tell your father.
I’m going to tell Santa Claus.
I’m not going to give you any candy.
I’m very angry now.
I’m going to give you a good smack.
I mean it.
I really mean it.
I’m not kidding.
(SMACK)

blocks.text: A Two Year Old in a Plane
The stewardess had a terrible time on a trip across the country. There was bad weather and the passengers were complaining.

There was a two year old child running up and down the aisle shouting and hitting people and making all sorts of noises. As he was running, he knocked the stewardess almost into the lap of a gentleman. The stewardess smile quietly and whispered in the child’s ear: «Little boy, why don’t you go and play outside?»

items.q: What sort of trouble was the stewardess having?
Why did the passengers feel annoyed?
Who is to blame for the child’s misbehavior?
Why do you think she told the child to go outside and play?
What threat do you usually use with your children, (if you have any)?
Discuss with your classmates, the most appropiate way to discipline a small child.
What would you do in case of a real discipline emergency?
How is curiosity different from misbehavior?
Were you curious as a child? What kind of trouble did your curiosity get you into?

blocks.title: Mom, I Want to Go Out

items: *Billy:* Mom.
*Mrs. White:* Yes, Billy?
*B:* I don’t feel like doing homework.
*Mrs. W:* Well that’s something you have to do, so you’d better start right now.
*B:* Oh, I’ve finished for tonight.
*Mrs. W:* What are you doing now?
*B:* Nothing. I’d like to go out and ride my bike.
*Mrs. W:* No, it’s too late, it’s quite dark.
*B:* I wish it was summer, so that I could go out after I’ve finished my homework.
*Mrs. W:* It will be summer sooner than you think, and please stop making that noise with your feet.
*B:* I wish I could find something to do.
*Mrs. W:* It’s a pity you don’t collect stamps any more.
*B:* I got tired of sticking little pieces of paper in an album.
*Mrs. W:* I bought that album for you because you kept asking for it. I wish I hadn’t bought it.
*B:* I’m sorry, mom. But I just want to do something different.
*Mrs. W:* O.K. Billy, I understand. Why don’t you join the Boy Scouts?
*B:* Gee! Are you sure I can?
*Mrs. W:* Quite sure. See the Scoutmaster about it tomorrow.
*B:* Can I go out and tell my friend Jack?
*Mrs. W:* No, Billy, It’s too late. Tell him about it tomorrow at school. You must go to bed in a minute.
*B:* I wish I didn’t have to go to bed at eight o’clock. I wish I was older!

blocks.title: Decide whether the following statements are TRUE or FALSE.

items.q: Billy feels happy about his homework.
He cannot ride his bike because it’s cold outside.
Billy used to collect stamps but he doesn’t like it any more.
His father gave him a stamp album.
His mother suggests that he becomes a boy scout.
Billy was allowed to go out and tell his friend Jack about his decision.
